rows.en: It seems to me that nowadays Americans cannot turn on the television or read a newspaper without seeing the word pop up somewhere as a description of the American demographic.
zh: 在我看来，如今美国人只要打开电视或翻开报纸，
就会在某处看到这个词，用来描述美国的人口构成。

rows.en: Well, at one time the US was called a melting pot, you know, which means that people of many different religions, cultures, and races could shed their traditional cultural identities and blend into one homogeneous nation.
rows.at: could shed their traditional cultural identities
zh: 嗯，美国曾被称为“大熔炉”，也就是说，信仰、文化和种族各不相同的人，
可以放下原有的传统文化身份，融合为一个同质的国家。

true_cut_word_anchors.at: could shed their traditional cultural identities

rows.en: Um, of course, when the phrase “melting pot” was popular, there was also the idea of being different, but being different then simply meant Catholic as opposed to Protestant, or Irish as opposed to Swedish or Italian.
zh: 嗯，当然，在“大熔炉”这个说法流行时，也存在差异的观念，
不过那时所谓的不同，只是天主教徒相对于新教徒，或者爱尔兰裔相对于瑞典裔、意大利裔的差别。

rows.en: You see today, we use the word diversity to refer to more-visible ethnic differences — Asian American, African American, and Latino, for instance.
zh: 你看，如今我们用“多样性”指更为明显的族裔差异，
例如亚裔美国人、非裔美国人以及拉丁裔。

rows.en: Well, I think in all this talk of diversity there is a critical point that may be missed: that is, diversity is not occurring everywhere in the US, or at least not to a degree that would alter the demography of every region in the country.
zh: 嗯，我认为，在所有这些关于多样性的讨论中，人们可能忽略了一个关键点：
多样化并未发生在美国所有地方，至少还没有达到改变全国每个地区人口构成的程度。

rows.en: On the contrary, Maine’s Caucasian population was 98% of its total population throughout the 1990s; and by 2025, Maine’s population will still be 97% Caucasian, which means virtually no change in Maine’s racial diversity over the next 20 or so years.
zh: 相反，整个20世纪90年代，缅因州的高加索裔人口占总人口的98%；到2025年，
这个比例仍将为97%，也就是说，在之后二十年左右的时间里，缅因州的种族多样性几乎不会发生变化。
